messages.subject: How to shift time of just some photos at a station?
messages.subject_clean: How to shift time of just some photos at a station?
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

i just started using camtrapR, i'm trying to organize raw images. I have the problem that, while the cameras were set on study area, some lost the initial configuration and restarted, so in some stations some picture have wrong time and date, while others pictures in the same station are fine.

TimeShiftedImages is a function that could help me, the problem is that it says: ..."timeshift is the amount by which to shift the time of all images at that station...", however i need to shift some, and not all date and time on images at the stations.

Could anyone help me on that?

Thank you!!

Regards,

José.

messages.subject: Re: How to shift time of just some photos at a station?
messages.subject_clean: How to shift time of just some photos at a station?
messages.body_plain:
Hi José,
as you said, this situation is a little different from what the function was intended for, but I think it can still be used:

Put all the images from a given station that need a time shift into a common directory within the station directory (like a camera directory)
When running timeShiftImages,set argument hasCameraFolders to TRUE and specify the directory in the timeShiftTable column "camera")

See data("timeShiftTable") for an example (you'd use the "camera" column), which is empty in the example.

It is not a pretty solution, but it should work.
Cheers,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: problem with exiftool
messages.body_plain:
Hi Angela,
I think exiftool is available. It looks more like a problem with your directory_original variable. Is it defined correctly?. Can you please show the content of that object?

See the last bit of your error message, the part I highlighted:

In addition: Warning messages:
1: running command 'exiftool -q -f -t -r -Directory -FileName -EXIF:DateTimeOriginal -ext JPG "NA"' had status 1
2: running command 'exiftool -q -f -t -r -Directory -FileName -EXIF:DateTimeOriginal -ext JPG ""' had status 1

Instead of "NA" or "", it should be a directory name (a station directory to be precise).
Jürgen
